question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is on bed rest notes a red area over his tail bone. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Leave the area and check next week
option_2: Rub the red area firmly each hour
option_3: Turn him often and keep the area clean and dry
option_4: Give a pain killer and let him rest
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Turn him often and keep the area clean and dry

Clinical Rationale: A red area over the tail bone in a man on bed rest points to early pressure damage, so he is turned often and the area kept clean and dry.

Key Clue: a red area over the tail bone in a man on bed rest

Priority Principle: Pressure care

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting a week lets the damage worsen; (b) Rubbing a red area harms the tissue more; (d) A pain killer does not help the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: The red area is rubbed firmly each hour.

5-Second Recall: Turn him often and keep the area clean and dry.

PNC Exam Pearl: Offload the spot, keep it dry.

question: A nurse caring for a man who has had a stroke notes he cannot swallow his own spit. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take FIRST?
option_2: Give him a big drink of water
option_3: Ask him to swallow hard
option_4: Turn him on his side and clear the mouth
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Turn him on his side and clear the mouth

Clinical Rationale: A stroke patient who cannot swallow his own spit may choke, so he is turned on his side and the mouth cleared.

Key Clue: a stroke patient who cannot swallow his own spit

Priority Principle: Stroke

Why Not Others: (a) Flat on his back lets the spit pool; (b) A big drink risks choking; (c) Swallowing hard may choke him.

PGI Exam Trap: He is left flat on his back.

5-Second Recall: Turn him on his side and clear the mouth.

PNC Exam Pearl: Side, clear the mouth.
